items.text: What statute lists the mandatory provisions every Michigan fire insurance policy must contain?

MCL 500.2833, titled Fire insurance policy; mandatory provisions; coverage. It lists 19 required provisions, lettered (a) through (s), plus a subsection (2) minimum tied to the former standard fire policy.
Where does MCL 500.2833 sit inside the Insurance Code, and when was it added?
Chapter 28, Fire Insurance Contracts (MCL 500.2804 to 500.2866), of the Insurance Code of 1956 (1956 PA 218). Added by 1990 Act 305, immediate effect December 14, 1990.
What is the statutory minimum coverage floor under MCL 500.2833(1)(a)?
Actual cash value (ACV) of the property at the time of the loss, subject to the policy's other provisions. A policy can promise more than ACV, but never less.
What does MCL 500.2833(1)(b) require as minimum peril coverage, and what removal coverage comes with it?
Direct loss by fire and lightning, plus pro rata coverage for 5 days for insured property removed to another location to preserve it from a covered peril.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(c), on what basis may a fire policy be void?
Misrepresentation, fraud, or concealment. The statute says the policy 'may' be void on this basis; the exact voidance language is set by the policy itself.
What must a fire policy state under MCL 500.2833(1)(d) and (1)(e)?
(d) what property is not covered under the policy, and (e) what perils are not covered under the policy.
What do MCL 500.2833(1)(f) and (1)(g) require a fire policy to include?
(f) the conditions that suspend or restrict coverage, and (g) a provision for waiving or changing a term of the policy.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(h), when the insured cancels a fire policy, what is the minimum earned premium the insurer keeps?
Not less than the pro rata premium for the expired time, or $25.00, whichever is greater.
A homeowner cancels a fire policy after only 5 percent of the term has run, and the pro rata premium share is $8. How much can the insurer keep as minimum earned premium under 2833(1)(h)?
$25.00. The statute sets the floor at the pro rata amount or $25, whichever is greater, so the $8 pro rata figure is overridden by the $25 minimum.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(i), how much advance written notice must an insurer mail before cancelling a fire policy?

Not less than 10 days before cancellation, mailed to each named insured at the last-known address, postage fully prepaid, with the same $25/pro rata minimum earned premium as an insured-initiated cancellation.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(j), how many days' notice must an insurer give a mortgagee before cancelling the mortgagee's interest in a fire policy?
Not less than 10 days' written notice, where loss is payable in whole or part to a mortgagee not named as an insured.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(j), if the insured fails to render proof of loss, how long does a notified mortgagee have to render its own proof of loss?
60 days after the notice.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(j), if the insurer pays a mortgagee but denies liability to the mortgagor or owner, what right does the insurer get?

The insurer is subrogated to the mortgagee's rights of recovery (both contract and tort claims, capped at the amount paid) without impairing the mortgagee's own right to sue; alternatively the insurer may pay off the mortgage debt and take an assignment of the debt and mortgage.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(k), how is the insurer's liability limited when other insurance also covers the peril?
The insurer's liability is no greater than its pro rata share alongside the other insurance covering the same peril.
What does MCL 500.2833(1)(l) require a fire policy to state?
The notification requirements the insured must follow when a loss occurs.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), who may demand an appraisal, and over what?
Either party (insured or insurer) may make a written demand for appraisal if they fail to agree on the actual cash value or the amount of the loss.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), how long does each side have to select and identify its own appraiser once a written appraisal demand is received?
20 days after receipt of the written demand.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), what happens if the two appraisers cannot agree on an umpire within 15 days?
Either the insured or the insurer may ask a circuit court judge, in the county where the loss occurred or the property is located, to select an umpire.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), how many of the three appraisal participants must sign a written agreement to set the amount of loss?
Any 2 of the 3 (the two appraisers, or one appraiser and the umpire). A written agreement signed by any 2 of the 3 sets the amount of the loss.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), how are appraisal costs split?
Each party pays its own appraiser. Other appraisal expenses and the umpire's compensation are split equally between the insured and the insurer.
TRAP: Under MCL 500.2833(1)(m), can an appraisal panel decide whether a disputed item is covered at all under the policy?

No. The statute limits appraisal to 'the amount of the loss or the actual cash value'; whether an item is covered at all is a coverage question for a court, not the panel (Maksym v Auto-Owners, COA published Feb 24 2026, No. 372827, developed in the appraisal domain).
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(n), what four options does the insurer have instead of simply paying cash?
The insurer may repair, replace, rebuild, or take the damaged property.
What does MCL 500.2833(1)(o) say about abandonment?
There can be no abandonment to the insurer of any property; the insured cannot hand over damaged property and treat it as a full loss by abandonment.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(p), how many days after receipt of proof of amount of loss is a fire loss payable?
30 days, except as otherwise provided in MCL 500.2845 (the municipal escrow-withholding statute).
TRAP: If a municipality is escrow-withholding funds under MCL 500.2845, does a payment delay past 30 days violate MCL 500.2833(1)(p)?
No. 2833(1)(p) expressly says the 30-day payment rule applies 'except as otherwise provided in section 2845,' so a 2845-authorized escrow delay is not a violation of the 30-day rule.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(q), how long after the loss must a suit under the policy be commenced?
Within 1 year after the loss, or within the time period specified in the policy, whichever is longer.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(q), when is the 1-year suit-limitation clock tolled, and until when?
It is tolled from the time the insured notifies the insurer of the loss until the insurer formally denies liability. Tolled means the clock stops running during that window.
TRAP: Under MCL 500.2833(1)(q), does the insured always have exactly 1 year from the date of loss to sue, no matter what the insurer does?

No. The 1-year (or longer policy period) clock is tolled from notice of loss until the insurer's formal denial, so the real filing deadline depends on how long the insurer takes to formally deny the claim.
What does MCL 500.2833(1)(r) require regarding subrogation?
That the insurer is subrogated to the insured's right of recovery from other parties responsible for the loss.
Under MCL 500.2833(1)(s), at what time does a fire insurance policy become effective?
12:01 a.m., standard time, at the location of the property involved.
What does MCL 500.2833(2) require as a coverage floor, beyond subsection (1)?
Except as otherwise provided in the Insurance Code, each fire policy under subsection (1) must contain, at minimum, the coverage provided in the standard fire policy under former MCL 500.2832.
What happened to former MCL 500.2832, and when?

It was repealed effective January 1, 1992, by 1990 Act 305 (the same act that added MCL 500.2833). The Michigan Legislature's site shows only the repeal notice and a one-line compiler's note that it 'pertained to form of standard policy.'
Under MCL 500.2845(1), what percentage of a fire-loss settlement must an insurer withhold in a qualifying (smaller-population) municipality?
25% of the actual cash value of the insured real property at the time of loss, or 25% of the final settlement, whichever is less.
What is the residential withholding dollar cap under MCL 500.2845, and how is it adjusted?
$12,000, effective beginning January 1, 2015, adjusted every January 1 according to the Consumer Price Index. Before 2015 the base was $6,000, itself CPI-adjusted annually from June 1, 1999.
MCL 500.2845 applies only to which Michigan municipalities?

Cities, villages, and townships in counties with a population under 425,000, excluding any such municipality that itself has 50,000 or more people, and only if the municipality has opted in with DIFS.
Under MCL 500.2845, how long does a municipality have to tell an insurer it wants the withheld amount escrowed, before the money defaults to the insured?
15 days after the mailing of the withholding notice; otherwise the withheld amount is paid to the insured 15 days after the notice.
Under MCL 500.2845, once a municipality escrows the withheld amount, how long does the insured have to object to the retention?
10 days from the date of mailing of the notice.
Under MCL 500.2845(7), what happens if no reasonable proof of repair or demolition is shown within 120 days after the treasurer receives the withheld funds?
The city, village, or township may use the retained proceeds itself to secure, repair, or demolish the damaged structure and clear the property to code, returning any unused portion to the insured.
Under MCL 500.2845(7), within how long must an insured sue a municipality to recover withheld policy proceeds?
Within 3 years after the insurer provided the original withholding notice to the insured.
Under MCL 500.2845, what settlement threshold must be exceeded before the withholding requirement even applies?
The final settlement must exceed 49% of the insurance on the insured real property.
Under MCL 500.2845(13), how can an insured avoid the 25% withholding entirely?

By filing evidence of a repair contract with the insurer within 15 days after the final settlement is agreed, consenting to pay the contractor directly, and having the insurer notify the municipality that there will be no withholding.
How does MCL 500.2227 relate to MCL 500.2845?

It is a structural twin (same 25% withholding, escrow, and proof mechanics) but for the opposite population band: larger counties or larger municipalities, versus 2845's smaller-population municipalities.
MCL 500.2227 applies to which Michigan municipalities?
Cities, villages, and townships in counties with a population of 425,000 or more, plus any city, village, or township of 50,000 or more even inside a smaller county.
What perils trigger the withholding requirement under MCL 500.2227(1), beyond fire?
Fire, explosion, vandalism, malicious mischief, wind, hail, riot, or civil commotion, a broader list than MCL 500.2845's fire-and-explosion-only trigger.
What did 2024 PA 82 change about the residential withholding cap under MCL 500.2227?
It raised the base cap from $12,000 to $24,000 beginning July 1, 2024, and changed the adjustment date to every July 1 by the Consumer Price Index (immediate effect July 23, 2024).
TRAP: Do MCL 500.2845 and MCL 500.2227 share the same dollar cap and adjustment date?

No. 2845 stays on its original $12,000 (2015) base, adjusted every January 1. 2227 was bumped to a $24,000 base by 2024 PA 82, effective July 1, 2024, and is adjusted every July 1. Never swap one section's figure for the other.
What is the Michigan fire-insurance maximum withholding amount under DIFS Bulletin 2026-16-INS, and for what period?
$25,090, effective July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
Which statute does DIFS Bulletin 2026-16-INS adjust, and who signed it?
MCL 500.2227 (not 500.2845). Issued and entered June 2, 2026, by Director Anita G. Fox; it supersedes Bulletin 2025-14-INS.
TRAP: A study guide says Bulletin 2026-16-INS sets a new withholding cap under MCL 500.2845. Correct this.
Wrong statute. Bulletin 2026-16-INS is issued under MCL 500.2227, the larger-municipality escrow statute, not MCL 500.2845. The two sections carry separate bulletins and separate dollar figures.
According to DIFS Bulletin 2026-16-INS, what was the fire-insurance maximum withholding amount for the prior period, July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026?
A homeowners policy's Conditions section has a clause titled 'Appraisal'. Which MCL 500.2833 subdivision sets the statutory floor that clause cannot go below?
Subdivision (m), the appraisal-demand and 20-day appraiser / 15-day umpire mechanics, each side paying its own appraiser and splitting the rest.
A homeowners policy's Conditions section has a clause titled 'Our Option'. Which MCL 500.2833 subdivision sets the statutory floor that clause cannot go below?
Subdivision (n), the insurer's option to repair, replace, rebuild, or take the damaged property instead of paying cash.
A homeowners policy's Conditions section has a clause titled 'Mortgage Clause'. Which MCL 500.2833 subdivision sets the statutory floor that clause cannot go below?
Subdivision (j), the mortgagee's 10-day cancellation notice and 60-day render-proof-of-loss mechanics, plus the insurer's subrogation rights against the mortgagee's recovery.
TRAP: A Michigan HO-3's 'Suit Against Us' condition gives the insured 2 years to sue. Under MCL 500.2833(1)(q), which controls, the statute's 1 year or the policy's 2 years?

The policy's 2 years. (q) says an action must be commenced within 1 year after the loss or within the period specified in the policy, whichever is longer. The statute is a floor: a policy may lengthen the window but can never shorten it below 1 year, and the notice-to-formal-denial tolling still applies.
How does MCL 500.2833(1)(j)'s mortgagee proof-of-loss mechanic affect a restoration contractor's job timeline?

Because loss checks are usually made jointly payable to insured and mortgagee, a slow or uncooperative insured can trigger a separate 60-day mortgagee proof-of-loss clock; a contractor tracking the job should know this clock exists and can flag delays to the homeowner.
Can a restoration contractor demand an appraisal under MCL 500.2833(1)(m) on the homeowner's behalf?

No. Appraisal is the insured's right to demand, not the contractor's; a contractor demanding or negotiating appraisal for a fee edges into unlicensed public adjusting under MCL 500.1222. The contractor's estimate can support the homeowner's own demand, but the demand itself belongs to the insured.
Why does MCL 500.2833(1)(p)'s 30-day payment rule matter for a restoration contractor's cash flow planning?

Once the insured supplies proof of the amount of loss, payment is due within 30 days (subject to any 2845 escrow delay), which sets the outer boundary a contractor can plan draw schedules and payment expectations against.
Why should a restoration contractor track MCL 500.2833(1)(q)'s 1-year, tolled suit clock even though the contractor is not a party to the policy?

Because a claim can head toward litigation while repairs are still being negotiated; the contractor's own project and lien timeline should be planned against the homeowner's outer legal deadline, so the homeowner's claim does not run out the clock mid-job.
Under MCL 500.2845(6), what counts as 'reasonable proof' that repair or demolition work has been done?

Verifiable contracts, invoices, and receipts; an affidavit from the contractor doing the most work, with attached contracts/invoices/receipts; or a municipal inspection of the property verifying the work.
